_about: One-hour executive briefing: the migration factory this repository implements for LabVIEW, C/C++ and MATLAB estates, drawn as flow diagrams. Build: python tools/build_deck.py templates/deck-exec-briefing.json templates/deck-exec-briefing.html. Speaker notes and timing: TALK-TRACK.md. Every number is quoted from python tools/golden_path.py, python tools/vi_fleet_scan.py (with lvkit 0.8.6 installed) or make -C templates/host-harness test; tools/tests/test_flow_deck.py pins them.
title: Three toolsets, one proven path
subtitle: How this repository takes a tree of .vi, .c and .m files to ported code with proof, one unit at a time. LabVIEW / TestStand, C/C++ firmware, MATLAB / Simulink. Offline, on a laptop, with Devin Desktop.
footer: Synthetic reference system, customer-neutral. Everything shown runs offline from this folder.

slides.notes: One hour: 50 minutes of slides, 10 for questions. Everything on these slides was produced by tools in this folder; nothing was typed from memory.

slides.notes: The picture to remember. Discovery is static evidence and orders the work; the gate in the middle is runtime proof and closes an item. Dashed box: designed, not merged.

slides.title: LabVIEW estate: from a folder of VIs to a proven rig
slides.caption: The scan orders the work: its classification is static evidence, not proof that anything ports. A rig is done when tools/bench_compare.py says PASS against the rig's own recording. Fixtures: example-system/fleet, example-system/real-vi, example-system/bench.
slides.notes: Workflows 9 then 6. A .vi is a proprietary binary; there is no point-and-convert step and the skill says so. The recording, not the source, is the proof.

slides.caption: Your C is compiled on a laptop against the stubbed HAL in templates/host-harness and tested there (on the example: host tests: 58 checks passed). The Python twin is a second implementation kept honest by the same tests and vectors. Nothing converts C to Python, and host tests do not prove target timing, interrupts or certification objectives.

slides.caption: Token use is bounded by the files, not by the prompt: the scanner reads the tree once and writes rows; each unit then gets one prompt carrying only its row. .github/workflows/check.yml already runs every check offline on Python 3.10 and 3.12 and keeps the proof as an artifact. Dashed boxes are designed in the research plan and not merged; the golden path will stop at 'prompt pack generated' and will not claim an agent ran.

slides.title: The evidence boundary: what each artefact lets you say
rows: Static: fleet classification
tools/vi_fleet_scan.py, lvkit describe / unresolved
How many VIs, what is in them, which to try first
That any VI ports; that is per-rig work
Static: firmware map, model notes
/bring-your-firmware, /matlab-to-code
Where the HAL seam is; which numeric rules apply
That the code is correct
Runtime: PASS from bench_compare.py
The port replayed on the recording or the vectors
The port reproduces every column of one real run
Behaviour on inputs that run never saw
Runtime: host tests
make -C templates/host-harness test
The logic passes nominal, fault and boundary cases
Target timing, interrupts, RTOS, silicon, certification
slides.note: Every skill prints its own boundary in its output; a port without a recording is labelled a draft.
slides.notes: Static evidence orders the work; runtime evidence closes an item. Keep the two words apart in every conversation.

slides.title: Retain, wrap or port: one answer per SubVI or block, reason recorded
rows: Port
Pure logic: sequencing, parsing, maths, verdicts, report generation
Python, proven against the recording
Wrap
Works, cannot be re-verified cheaply, or needs an NI driver you keep (DAQmx, VISA)
Python calls the VI, executable or instrument; Python owns sequencing and results
Retain
FPGA, Real-Time targets, hardware-timed loops, anything the recording cannot exercise
Stays in LabVIEW; Python consumes its output files
Unreadable
No lvkit, no HTML export, no screenshots yet
A backlog row asking for the export before anyone estimates
slides.note: Source: .devin/skills/labview-to-python/SKILL.md and .devin/skills/vi-fleet-discovery/SKILL.md; the fleet scanner proposes, the per-rig review decides.
slides.notes: The answer that surprises people is Retain: the goal is a bench you can trust, not zero LabVIEW.

slides.title: What Devin with this repository adds over a general coding agent
slides.left_title: A general agent on the same tree
left: Reads what fits in one prompt and re-reads the tree every session
Writes code that looks right; the proof is whatever you remember to ask for
Blurs the boundary: a reading of a diagram presented as behaviour
One-off session; nothing for the next person to rerun
right: The scanner reads the whole tree once; each unit gets one bounded prompt
Every lane ends in bench_compare.py or make test saying PASS or FAIL per column
Skills print what is not proven, in their own output, every run
Skills, tracker, backlog and deck rebuild offline from plain CSV and JSON anyone can open
slides.notes: Devin Desktop plus this folder. No cloud service is required for any step shown today.

slides.title: What is not covered, said before you ask
bullets: No .vi to Python converter: a VI is a proprietary binary; lvkit gives inventory and drawings, never the deliverable
No C to Python converter: the Python twin is a second implementation kept honest by shared tests
Host tests do not prove target timing, interrupts, RTOS scheduling, DMA, power modes, MISRA or DO-178C objectives
Vector equivalence does not prove the design, only that the code matches the model on those rows
Without a recording a LabVIEW port is a draft, and the skill labels it as one
Repo-scale MATLAB and C scanners, the prompt pack and the pipeline runner are designed, not merged
No TestStand or TDMS file ships here; the real-VI lane stops at the diagram reading until someone records a run
slides.notes: Read this slide slowly. It is the slide that earns trust.

slides.title: Day one on your tree: the commands
bullets: python tools/doctor.py   (is this laptop ready? prints READY)
python tools/golden_path.py   (every workflow end to end, offline; proof left in outputs/golden/)
python tools/vi_fleet_scan.py <your tree> --name <estate>   (inventory CSV + migration backlog)
/labview-to-python <rig export or .vi> <recording.csv>   (one rig, proven against its recording)
/bring-your-firmware <your C tree>   (map, host harness, first three tests)
slides.note: Then: /track-and-report and /exec-deck read those files; ask for the end result and Devin runs the whole row (WORKFLOWS.md).
slides.notes: If there is time, run python tools/vi_fleet_scan.py example-system --name demo-fleet live and open the backlog.

slides.text: The recording, not the source, is the proof. Inventory tells you where to start; a comparison tells you when you are done.
